sentences.text: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 18.08.2022 at about 10.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EF- 5814, near Satyamma Temple, Andarlahalli Gate, Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura Hobli.
At that time another motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-03-JH-3573 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner resulting in accident.
Due to said accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his right leg, shoulder and other injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was taken to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital, wherein first aid was given and later got shifted to Sri. Sathya Sai Memorial hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient and spent .3,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Photography and earning .20,000/- to .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Avenger motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. The petition against respondent No.1 is dismissed for default as the petitioner not taken effective steps for service of notice.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal, in-spite of service of notice, hence he has been placed ex-parte.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, the below mentioned points arise for consideration:
POINTS

1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 18.08.2022 at about 10.30 p.m., Near Satyamma Temple, Andarlahalli Gate, Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura Hobli, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EF-5814, due to the rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-03-JH-3573 by its rider?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
5. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.

The petitioner contended that on 18.08.2022 at about 10.30 p.m., accident occurred when the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EF-5814 near Satyamma Temple, Andarlahalli Gate, Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura Hobli, due to the rash and negligent riding another motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-03-JH-3573 by its rider in which he sustained grievous injuries.
9. In order to prove rash and negligent riding of offending motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-03-JH- 3573 by its rider, the petitioner got examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider, the accident occurred.
PW.1 is not cross examined on behalf of respondents.
The respondent No.2 not appeared before the Tribunal in order to controvert the claim of petitioner.

Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed any satisfactory materials to rebut the evidence of PW.1.
10.

Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2, first information statement, lodged by the petitioner with the police on 19.08.2022 with respect to the accident.
On the basis of first information lodged by complainant, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the complaint as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex . P.4
discloses the aspect of damages caused to the offending vehicle.
The rider or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicles.
The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 and 338 of IPC and U/s.181, 196 of M.V.Act, which is marked as Ex.P.6.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

The police filed the final report after detailed Gajendra Babu N.S vs Syed Avaize on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12455823/
3 investigation.

sentences.text: The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The rider or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondent neither appeared nor placed any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
11. The respondents neither appeared nor placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of offending vehicle has driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner that resulted in the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced by petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-03-JH-3573 by its rider and same resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Point No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Point No.2:
In view of holding point No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.

13. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained grievous injuries to his right leg,
shoulder and other injuries all over the body.
In order to prove the injuries, petitioner has produced Ex.P.5 - wound certificate issued by Chikkaballapura Government Hospital, wherein first aid was given.

The materials on record disclose that the petitioner later shifted to Sri.Sathya Sai Memoraial Hospital wherein he appears to have admitted as an inpatient and underwent closed reduction and I.M Newlong on 01.09.2022 and underwent drill bit removal on 08.09.2022 and discharged on 10.09.2022 with an advise for regular follow up and bed rest.
As per the said document, the doctor opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner produced Ex.P.7 - OPD, issued by Chikkaballapur Institute of Medical Sciences and Teaching Hospital.

sentences.text: In order to prove disability, the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contention related to disability stated to have been caused due to the accident.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to ascertain and adjudicate the aspect of disability, as contended by him.
The petitioner produced medical bills amounting to .1,500/- which are marked as Ex.P.7.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut the medical bills furnished by petitioner.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the aspect of disability.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .1,00,000/-.
14.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
The petition against respondent No.1 is dismissed for default as the petitioner not taken effective steps for service of notice.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-03-JH-3573 by its rider.
The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective policy of insurance at the time of accident.
Respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending vehicle and appears to be in charge of the vehicle at the time of accident.
So, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Point No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Point No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said points, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
The petition against respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

Respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
